passages.text: The state-existence problem is already easy in several explicit ZF carriers. The next scientific question is which physical assumptions select a state. Candidate selectors include a Hamiltonian ground condition, KMS condition, incoming detector preparation, residual symmetry, or a local Hadamard condition. Each should be tested independently for existence, uniqueness, foundational strength, and compatibility with gauge structure. A no-selection theorem is valuable only when its symmetry and state class are physically justified.
